title: Tambuli Upo: Characteristics
metaDescription: Tambuli upo is an open pollinated upo variety from Allied Botanical (Condor). See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Tambuli upo is an open pollinated upo variety, also sold or known as Tambuli bottle gourd. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor).

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Tambuli upo is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Tambuli bottle gourd, this is the same upo. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [upo variety finder](/crop-varieties/upo), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 55 to 60 days after sowing, Ramgo's packet gives 50 to 55 days. Yield, by the seller's count: 15 to 20 t/ha potential (Ramgo packet figure). No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit upo fields most often: [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 55 to 60 days after sowing, Ramgo's packet gives 50 to 55 days.
**Fruit:** Stout, heavy, cylindrical and light green, about 26 cm long and 2 to 3 kg.
**Season:** All year (Allied), Ramgo lists its packet for the dry season.
Intermediate resistance to cucumber mosaic virus (Allied).

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the long standing open pollinated upo: in the upo table, packed by both Condor/Allied and Ramgo (garden packet), and stocked by online agri stores. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual upo on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Tambuli upo

Upo grows fast on a trellis. Pick a variety with a smooth, even fruit that stays tender, and harvest it young. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Tambuli bottle gourd the same as Tambuli?
items.a: Yes. Tambuli bottle gourd is another name for Tambuli. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Tambuli?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
